title: Prefill Orchestration Sprint 48 — Ops Journal
content:
Sprint 48 ops journal — prefill orchestration and kernel-batching sync

Attendees: Aisha (owner), Miguel, Claire, Omar, Dana (SRE drop-in)
Date range: 2028-03-15 through 2028-03-22
Channel: #serving-runtime-prefill (standup notes captured)

TL;DR
- Prefill orchestration prototype (v0.6) landed on staging; initial micro-benchmarks show 8–12% P95 token latency regression under extreme micro-batching compared to v0.5 but ~20% lower tail for small-seq requests due to better KV reuse.
- KV eviction bug surfaced in production canary (INF-2143) — root cause: eviction race when slot reallocation coincided with async prefill completion. Hotfix rolled to canary, patch PR ready.
- Decided to throttle prefill commits from background workers when kernel load > 70% to avoid eviction oscillation.

Notes / narrative
- Monday: landed prefill-orch v0.6 to staging. Miguel ran the cross-traffic replay (replay-id: replay/2028-03-16-07) to simulate evening traffic. Observed improved prefix hit-rate (cache warmup from 18% -> 37%), which explains reduced P50 for short sequences.
- Tuesday: Claire noticed intermittent 503s on canary (#canary-2) tied to KV slot reallocation. Error trace points to async task completing after slot marked free -> double-free semantics. Put quick guard in allocator to fence async completion (PR 1329).
- Wednesday: Night spike reproduced the race in canary; rolled hotfix to canary and throttled prefill-commit rate by 3x. SRE monitored for 24h with no replication of the 503s.
- Thursday: Kernel batching policy experiments: tested 'aggressive-coalesce' vs 'steady-window' on staging. Aggressive gave slightly better throughput but higher P95 jitter when sequence length variance was high. We favored steady-window for now.
- Friday: Sync with product: new customer workload (low-latency chat) expected next month. We must keep small-seq latencies low; action items set to tighten backpressure thresholds and add a KV shadow-mode to validate no regressions on real traffic.

Quantitative snapshot (staging, replay load):
- baseline (v0.5): P50=22ms, P95=86ms, tail-99=210ms, cache-hit=18%
- v0.6 (prefill-orch enabled): P50=19ms, P95=92ms, tail-99=198ms, cache-hit=37%
- note: P95 regression driven by a subset of long-seq requests during aggressive coalescing window.

Incidents and triage
- Incident INF-2143: KV evict/double-free leading to transient 503s
  - timeline: detection 2028-03-17 03:14 UTC, mitigation 2028-03-17 04:02 UTC (throttle + guard fence), root cause analysis completed 2028-03-18.
  - root cause: asynchronous prefill completion callback could run after slot metadata was reset by concurrent eviction path. Missing lifecycle handoff in allocator.
  - fix: add completion fencing and CAS on slot state; backport to 0.5 for immediate patch; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1329
  - postmortem note: add unit tests that simulate delayed async completions (deterministic scheduler) and add a canary test that runs for 6h under synthetic slot thrash.

Experiments in flight
- Experiment: 'steady-window' kernel coalescing parameters (window_ms=6, max_batch=48). Goal: reduce P95 jitter for long-seq paths. Instrumentation: per-batch seq-variance histogram.
- Experiment: 'kv-prefill-shadow' — shadow prefill in staging against production traces, but do not commit; verifies prefill decisions and measures wasted compute. Running nightly for 72h; early data shows wasted prefill compute ~4% of baseline but with 25% higher hit-rate on subsequent requests.
- Profiling: microkernel hotpath — observed a hotspot in memcpy during KV merge on A100s; Miguel will prototype a flatten+memmove path to reduce allocations (Jira INF-2187).

Decisions made
- Keep steady-window coalescing in default staging config for next two weeks.
- Implement prefill commit throttling when kernel busy > 70% (setpoint to be tuned).
- Backport allocator fencing fix to v0.5 and schedule a canary rollout.

Action items (owners + ETA)
- Miguel: land allocator fencing hotfix to stable branch and deploy to canary (ETA 2028-03-24). linked: INF-2143, PR 1329.
- Claire: add deterministic async-completion unit tests + schedule 6h canary burst test (ETA 2028-03-28).
- Omar: run longer kv-prefill-shadow nightly for another week and produce cost vs hit-rate report (ETA 2028-03-30).
- Aisha: tune prefill throttle knobs (initial conservative threshold: kernel_load>70%) and add metrics dashboard (ETA 2028-03-26).
- Dana (SRE): create alerting rule for slot double-free rate > 0.1% in 10m window and add runbook section for eviction race (ETA 2028-03-25).

Blockers / open questions
- How aggressive can we be with prefill without increasing net compute cost beyond customer SLO? (need cost model from Optimize)
- Should we consider a two-tier KV slot marking (soft-locked vs hard-locked) to reduce eviction contention? Prototyping notes welcome.
- Need clarity from product about spike-resilience vs unit-cost tradeoffs for the upcoming customer workload.

Notes to self / low-priority items
- Follow up on memcpy hotspot: test with CUDA-aware buffer pooling; check alignment on 256B boundaries.
- Consider adding a lightweight per-request fingerprint to help correlate prefill decisions with resulting cache hits.

Appendix: quick links and traces
- Canary logs (error trace): /logs/canary-2/2028-03-17/trace-321987
- Replay metadata: replay/2028-03-16-07 (staging bucket)
- Related Jira: INF-2143, INF-2187
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1329

End of week impression: We made pragmatic progress — prefills are promising for small-seq latency improvements, but orchestration edge cases (eviction races) are an operational risk. Priority next week is to harden the allocator lifecycle and validate throttling knobs against longer canary runs.

-- Aisha
